messages:
ana: Quick check — are audit/event logs available as a near-real-time stream for ops? Need to wire up alerting for Permission_CHANGE events. Any existing kafka/topic or only batch S3 exports?

sam: We expose daily S3 exports (parquet) per-tenant: s3://redwood-audit/tenants/<tenant-id>/YYYY-MM-DD/*.parquet. For enterprise customers we can enable a Kafka topic (managed) that streams change events.

jess: +1 on kafka. If we enable that, what fields are redacted by default? We can't send raw user emails to external topics.

leo: Default pipeline redacts: full_email, ssn, and any field flagged as pii in the schema. We also have a 'minimal' schema that strips user identifiers entirely.

ana: Awesome. Would kafka stream have same retention as S3? Ops wants 90d lookback.

sam: Kafka retention is configurable per-tenant. Our hosted plan usually 7d; enterprise can request 90d with storage add-on. S3 exports are kept 1y by default (can be shortened).

mia: Reminder: enabling stream requires an access approval + network review. See process: ENGSEC-423. @tom can help with approvals.

tom: Yep — to start we'll need a submitted request in the audit-exports queue with tenant id, desired retention, and destination (kafka cluster or S3). I'll also ask infra for a VPC peering checklist.

ana: For alerting we only need Permission_CHANGE events. Can we filter at source so only those events go to the topic (and avoid PII transit)?

sam: Yes — we support per-topic event filters. You can request a 'Permission_CHANGE only' stream; the system will apply schema-level redaction and then forward. Example config snippet:
```
stream: kafka
topic: tenant-123.permission_changes
filter: event_type == "Permission_CHANGE"
redaction_profile: minimal
```

jess: Will QA see the same filtered stream? Need to ensure devs can replay events for debugging without exposing PII.

leo: We provide a replay token that gives time-limited access to a replay endpoint which returns filtered events. For deeper debugging we can provide a redacted debug bundle in S3 (ops-approved).

ana: Great. Last q — format of messages in kafka? Avro/JSON? What's schema evolution story?

sam: Kafka uses Avro with Confluent schema registry. We publish clear semantic versioning for schemas and a changelog. Backwards compatible changes only without a coordinated rollout.

ana: Thanks all — filing the org request now. cc @sec-bot for audit trail :eyes:
